juce.verified: 2026-09-04: tracktion_engine 0e02f70 pins modules/juce at exactly this commit

protobuf.note: C++ runtime and protoc for the engine, built from the submodule; the engine's CMake generates song.proto and render.proto at build time (ADR 0008 §4, pinned 2026-09-06). The last line before abseil, and what Ubuntu 24.04 packages. Added in M1 PR 5 as a new dependency, signed off 2026-09-07 (CLAUDE.md #4).

abseil.note: grpc's own third_party/abseil-cpp, pinned by the grpc commit above as juce is pinned by tracktion_engine's. Not a separate submodule of ours. sfizz-ui vendors abseil of the same LTS release inside its own ExternalProject, which is a separate CMake tree, so the two never meet.

grpc.note: grpc++ for the engine's Render and Preview services at M2 (ADR 0013 §1). Chosen as the NEWEST release whose own third_party/protobuf submodule is f0dc78d7e6e331b8c6bb2d5283e06aa26883ca7c — byte for byte the `protobuf` entry above — so gRPC's protobuf and ours are one pin rather than two that must agree. v1.52.2 and earlier pin v21.9; v1.55.0 pins protobuf 22.x, where abseil becomes protobuf's own dependency and ADR 0008 §4's reason for the v21.12 pin stops holding. Verified 2026-09-07: configured and built libgrpc++.a and grpc_cpp_plugin against engine/vendor/protobuf itself under -march=x86-64 -mtune=generic -ffp-contract=off (1345 targets, 2m53s on 20 jobs), emitting no -ffast-math, no second -march, and only the -maes/-msse4.1 on abseil's randen that engine/cmake/check_flags.cmake already allows. Integrated 2026-09-09 in M2 PR 9, which answered both of the questions this note left open. Coexistence: grpc's cmake/protobuf.cmake adds PROTOBUF_ROOT_DIR unconditionally in `module` mode, so gRPC owns the ONE add_subdirectory of our protobuf and the engine's own was removed; protoc consequently lives at engine/build/vendor/grpc/third_party/protobuf/protoc. Cost on two cores (pinned, g++ 13.3): 13m24s cold for all 1741 targets of which 2m08s is the protobuf this build already compiled, so gRPC's own addition is 11m16s — grpc 9m38s, abseil 53s, BoringSSL 31s, re2 12s, c-ares and zlib under 5s each — and 6.1s warm from a populated ccache. Approved as a dependency under CLAUDE.md #4. Named since PR 9 by tests/renders.rs's COMPONENTS and the engine job's component list, so a drift in this pin fails naming the component (ADR 0008 §5).

rubberband.note: time-stretch (GPL-2.0-or-later; compatible with this repository's AGPL-3.0 through the 'or later'). Options pinned in full by ADR 0011 §3: all twelve groups written out, which comes to OptionEngineFiner | OptionThreadingNever with the other ten at their zero defaults. Vendored 2026-09-07 in M1 PR 8 as a submodule, built from upstream's single/RubberBandSingle.cpp — one source file that hard-defines USE_BUILTIN_FFT and USE_BQRESAMPLER, so the FFT is not chosen from what the build machine has installed, and NO_THREADING, so ADR 0009 §3's single thread is compiled in as well as requested (ADR 0009 §4).

sfizz.note: library and JACK client only; this repo builds no VST3 (spike, 2026-09-04). The bundled plugin is sfizz_ui, and this entry documents what sfizz_ui vendors rather than a submodule of ours. Verified 2026-09-06 (M1 PR 6): sfizz-ui 6ef7b89 pins its `library` submodule at exactly this commit, so the two agree and sfizz_ui governs.

sfizz_ui.note: the sfizz VST3, and the submodule the engine builds. Added at M1 (ADR 0010); the `sfizz` pin alone builds none. Vendored 2026-09-06 in M1 PR 6, with surge_xt and dexed.

airwindows.note: deferred to M4 with clap-wrapper: an effect set, and its pinned repo may not build a Linux VST3 (ADR 0003 §4 amended, ADR 0010 §5).

app._note: app/'s direct dependencies, enumerated by exact version the way `schema` is, with the tree's integrity hashes in app/package-lock.json (docs/specs.md §17, registry packages). Signed off as ONE set under CLAUDE.md #4 (ADR 0016 §2); anything beyond this list goes back to a person before it is installed. Deliberately absent, each with its cost written out in ADR 0016 §3: any state library, any test framework, any CSS or component framework, and @vitejs/plugin-react. No app.* package can reach a render, so §17's golden-render pass is vacuous here and says so rather than being skipped (ADR 0016 §4). Written 2026-09-07 in M2 PR 1; installed 2026-09-07 in M2 PR 2, which wrote app/package.json against exactly this list and committed app/package-lock.json beside it: 106 entries, of which 64 are the per-platform binaries of esbuild, rolldown, lightningcss and @tauri-apps/cli that npm records and does not install, leaving 42 packages actually resolved on a Linux x86-64 install. Two entries the list does not name and PR 2 added anyway, both of them halves of things already here rather than new choices: tauri-build 2.6.3, Tauri's own build script crate, which is what tauri::generate_context! expands against; and @escribass/schema as a `file:../schema` link, which is this repository's own generated TypeScript and the only way to obey §4.1's ban on hand-written model types.

tauri.note: one Rust crate and two npm packages on separate version lines. The webview Tauri renders in — WebKitGTK, WKWebView, WebView2 — ships with the operating system and cannot be pinned by anyone (ADR 0016 §5).

vite.note: the one build dependency. React ships CommonJS and bare specifiers do not resolve in a browser, so tsc plus an import map is more configuration than a bundler, not less.

codemirror.note: no consumer until M4's code views (ADR 0003 §8). Pinned now anyway: it replaces `"6.x"`, which was not a pin and would have re-resolved silently on the first install.

_reused.note: already pinned under `schema.typescript`; app/ is a new consumer, not a new dependency. @bufbuild/protobuf is the runtime the generated TypeScript imports; tsx runs the projection golden under node:test (ADR 0012 §5), and @types/node is what lets `tsc --noEmit` check the file that imports node:test, node:assert and node:fs — added 2026-09-08 in M2 PR 4 (ADR 0016 §2, amended). None of the four reaches a runtime this build ships except @bufbuild/protobuf, and none can reach a render (ADR 0016 §4).

ai._note: The Python sidecar (docs/specs.md §6, §17). Written 2026-09-21 in M3 PR 2 from the user's decisions of 2026-09-17: U3 (the model is recorded, not pinned) and U4 (the packages, by name). Three packages are approved and carry `version: null` on purpose — U4 pins each 'by exact version when it is first added, not before', and nothing is installed until M3 PR 5, which writes the exact versions here, in §17 and in ai/uv.lock in one change; the file's own idiom for a pin that is owed is `null` with a note, as clap_sdk and faust below. No package here can reach a render (§17's last rule, ADR 0016 §4): the sidecar is audio-agnostic (CLAUDE.md #6) and everything it does to a song is a tool call.

python.note: exact patch in ai/.python-version from M3 PR 5 (§17)

ai.model_note: A RECORD, NOT A PIN (ADR 0021 §4; docs/specs.md §17, amended). A hosted model changes under its name and nothing can verify one, so this is the default a project records in its own lock.json `ai.model` on first use, and every log entry's `provenance.model_id` records what actually answered. Chosen by the user after the M3 spike and measured before it was recorded (2026-09-17: 45/45 on the nine feasible instructions, 5.8% refused calls all recovered, $0.0014 an edit at the median, and the same wrong-parameter mistake on `set_param` that withholding the tool removes). Cost and latency are properties of OpenRouter's routing, not of the name. Never counted by any 'verified' readout (docs/plan.md, M3 trap 15).

grpclib.note: The Python gRPC stack, decided by what the pinned betterproto2-compiler 0.10.1 generates: an async grpclib client AND server under client_generation=async, server_generation=async; a synchronous grpcio client and no server otherwise. `ai` serves (ADR 0020 §1), so grpclib it is, as betterproto2's `grpclib` extra plus the package (ADR 0020 §2). No grpcio, no grpcio-tools. The spike's scratch environment used 0.4.9; the pin is PR 5's.

openai.note: The OpenRouter client — §6's 'OpenAI-compatible client', literally. Approved 2026-09-17 (U4). The sidecar passes the key and base_url explicitly, because the SDK otherwise reads OPENAI_API_KEY. The spike ran 3.14.1; the pin is PR 5's.

httpx2.note: What the openai SDK carries today: a differently named package from httpx, which the first approval named and the spike corrected; approved by name 2026-09-17 (U4). The spike saw 2.13.0; the pin is PR 5's.

app and engine.grpc added 2026-09-07 in M2 PR 1 (ADR 0013 §1, ADR 0016). The frontend set is one sign-off; the golden-render pass is required of any pin that can reach a render, and app.* cannot.

ai filled in 2026-09-21 in M3 PR 2 (ADR 0020 §2, ADR 0021 §4): the model is a record and not a pin, and the three packages carry null until M3 PR 5 installs them, per U4's 'when it is first added, not before'. None can reach a render.

tool_api.python added 2026-09-22 in M3 PR 3 (ADR 0006 §7, ADR 0020 §1). Nothing new is pinned and nothing is installed: it records a third consumer of schema's already-pinned Python codegen, as tool_api.typescript records a second consumer of the TypeScript one. It cannot reach a render.

schema._note: Build-time codegen for schema/*.proto; none of it ships in the built product. Registry packages are pinned by exact version per docs/specs.md §17, with integrity hashes in Cargo.lock, package-lock.json and uv.lock.

betterproto2_compiler.note: runtime and compiler minor versions must match; pre-1.0, pin exactly

tool_api._note: The M0.3 tool API: the SongTools gRPC service and the MCP server (ADR 0006). Unlike `schema`, these ship in the built product; §17's registry-package rule covers them, with integrity hashes in Cargo.lock.

tonic_prost.note: requires prost ^0.14 and tonic ^0.14.6; tonic 0.13 pairs with prost 0.13 and would put a second prost::Message in the tree, which the generated Song would not satisfy

prost_types.note: direct dependency of the proto crate for FileDescriptorSet decoding; already present transitively via pbjson-types

sha2.note: content hashing for `add_asset` (M1 PR 3, ADR 0011): core hashes what enters the project. The engine hashes its own output, the PCM, with juce::SHA256 from the JUCE already pinned — the spike's note that it need not was about dependency count, and juce_cryptography adds none (ADR 0009 §2, settled 2026-09-06)

protoc_gen_tonic.note: codegen plugin, cargo install; requires protoc-gen-prost ^0.5.0, which is the pinned one. Rejects the btree_map option, which is prost's business anyway. The CI cache key in .github/workflows/checks.yml names the plugin set and changed with it

typescript._note: The service's TypeScript, generated since 2026-09-08 in M2 PR 3 — the milestone ADR 0006 §7 deferred it to, once `app` existed to consume it. Nothing new is pinned: protoc-gen-es writes it and @bufbuild/protobuf is what it imports, and both are already pinned under `schema.typescript` at the versions below. `proto` is a new consumer, not a new dependency — the same relationship `app._reused` records — so this needs no sign-off under CLAUDE.md #4. It is written down anyway because proto/AGENTS.md's "adding a language target" checklist asks for the version here, and because a reader of §17 should be able to see that the tool API has a second language target without reading a buf.gen.yaml. The tree's integrity hashes are in proto/package-lock.json: two runtime packages and a `file:../schema` link, which is all the generated code imports. `tsc` is not a dependency of `proto` at all — schema's pinned one is pointed at it.

python._note: The service's Python, generated since 2026-09-22 in M3 PR 3 — the milestone ADR 0006 §7 deferred it to, narrowed by ADR 0020 §1 to server_generation=async and client_generation=none because `ai` serves Assistant and dials nothing. Nothing new is pinned: betterproto2-compiler writes it and betterproto2 with pydantic is what it imports, and all three are already pinned under `schema.python` at the versions below, run out of schema/'s environment by `uv run --project ../schema`. `proto` is a new consumer, not a new dependency — the same relationship `typescript._reused` records — so this needs no sign-off under CLAUDE.md #4; it is written here because proto/AGENTS.md's 'adding a language target' checklist asks for the version, and because a reader of §17 should see that the tool API has a third language target without reading a buf.gen.yaml. Two things this target does NOT bring. The generated AssistantBase imports `grpclib`, which is `ai`'s package and is deliberately unpinned and uninstalled until M3 PR 5 (see `ai.grpclib`), so this code is regenerated and compared byte for byte by proto/codegen.sh --check and is imported and type-checked by nothing until then — a deferred check, recorded as one in docs/plan.md's ledger so PR 5 is obliged to close it. And betterproto2 has no extern_path, so it re-emits song.proto and history.proto; codegen.sh deletes that copy and rewrites the imports to escribass_schema, because a second Song in the tree is CLAUDE.md #1's failure in a fourth language (ADR 0020 §1, amended).

ci._note: GitHub Actions used by .github/workflows/. Build-time only; pinned by major version per the registry-package rule in docs/specs.md §17.

node.note: major pin; lock.baseline.json schema.typescript.node records the local 25.6.1

golden_render._note: What every M1 golden render is valid for (ADR 0009 §1, §5). ubuntu-latest moves, and every golden would drift with no PR to blame, so the engine and render jobs name the image explicitly.
golden_render.flags: -march=x86-64 -mtune=generic -ffp-contract=off on every vendored source, the three bundled plugins included; no -ffast-math and no second -march, checked against compile_commands.json by engine/cmake/check_flags.cmake before the engine and each plugin compiles (ADR 0009 §3; baseline chosen in M1 PR 5, extended to the plugins in PR 6, where the guard fired on sfizz's own -ffast-math and the flag was removed rather than the guard weakened)
